selection_notes: Candidates were mined by one agent. Each selected proof was re-run or re-read by the main session before selection, against the commit itself.
Preference went to cases whose finder is known from the fix commit message: selected defects were found by Codex, by a test or wiring proof, by the founder, or by the gate refusing real work.

No selected fix came from Gemini or Argon. Checked: the fix message, the spec under features/, and .finish-reviewed rows for the P-number. CF-3's spec records Gemini findings on its spec draft, none on this block.
The set is deliberately selected to include context-dependent defects. A win here justifies a follow-up, not a claim about reviews overall.

cases.head: 34baea34b217f9c9b722e53cc0c92438ddc8ac42
cases.defect: isPast in EventDetail.tsx is redefined from the event's real end to start + 12h. The host's Edit and Cancel controls, gated on !isPast elsewhere in that file, inherit the wider window, so a host can edit or cancel an event that already finished.
cases.evidence: src/app/prototypes/events/components/EventDetail.tsx:449 and :469 (isHost && !isPast), outside the hunks. Redefinition in the hunk at :189. EVENT_GRACE_HOURS = 12 at src/app/data/events-service-real.ts:35.
cases.proof: Source counterexample, re-read 2026-11-05: event with durationMinutes=90, viewed 2 hours after start by its host. isPast = now >= start + 12h = false, so :469 renders Edit and Cancel on a finished event. Before the commit, isPast was endDate < now, which is true.
cases.found_by: Codex review of the P1256 diff (fix message)
cases.why_chosen: A changed value whose consumers sit elsewhere in the same file.

cases.head: d4a03bfde56e87db83ca52b9d4a9ab3e73278d55
cases.defect: The ratchet block is written as a bare RATCHET_OUT="$(...)" followed by RATCHET_RC=$?. The hook runs under set -e, so a ratchet exit of 1 ends the hook at the assignment. The finding-printing and could-not-run branches never run and the commit is blocked with no message.
cases.evidence: scripts/pre-commit-checks.sh:6 (set -e), outside the hunks; the string set -e appears nowhere in the diff. Block in the hunk at about :166-167.
cases.proof: Failure demonstration, run 2026-11-05: bash -c 'set -e; O="$(bash -c "echo finding; exit 1")"; RC=$?; echo "unreached RC=$RC"' exits 1 and prints nothing.
cases.found_by: The final wiring proof (fix message and spec)
cases.why_chosen: One line far from the hunk decides what the hunk does. The pattern is common, so the scorer records whether set -e is cited.

cases.head: f14b0e53decd9686514fad8b93fbabcdb643f4ff
cases.defect: The new Back cache writer stores on-screen lists under the current profile's key, while the profile load chain has no cancellation on its full-load path. A slow load for profile A that lands after navigating to B writes A's rows onto B and caches them under B's key, so Back to B serves A's content with no refetch.
cases.evidence: src/app/pages/profile-page-v2.tsx: the Promise.all(...).then(...) chain from about :378 to :549 has no cancelled check and returns no cleanup on this path, outside the hunks. Writer in the hunk at about :560-575.
cases.proof: Source counterexample, re-read 2026-11-05: open /p/A, navigate to /p/B while A's Promise.all is pending (same component instance, effect re-runs). A's .then calls setRealStories/setRealPoints with A's rows, sets dataGenerationRef and setContentLoading(false). The writer effect then fires with cacheKey = B's path and writes those rows.
cases.oracle_note: The race predates the commit as a screen-only flash. The commit is what makes it persist, through the cache.
cases.found_by: Codex review, verified by the coordinator (fix message)
cases.why_chosen: A new cache makes an old race stick; the race lies outside the hunks in a changed file.

cases.head: c5803784ebc4440093e5f4cd76628f6d7131e6f6
cases.defect: Removing !isEmbed so point embeds expand inline leaves the sibling condition (liveSessionMode || profileOwner). The embed route passes no profileOwner unless the URL has ?from=, so the toggle flips to expanded and nothing renders.
cases.evidence: src/app/pages/point-detail-page.tsx:306-332 and :385 (embedProfileOwner built only from searchParams.get('from')), an unchanged file. Gate in the hunk.
cases.proof: Source counterexample, re-read 2026-11-05: /point/<id>?embed=true with no from. fromHolder is undefined, embedProfileOwner is undefined, liveSessionMode is not set, so storiesExpanded=true renders no block.
cases.why_chosen: Tiny diff; the whole question is what the caller passes.

cases.head: 2f6d56beeb4c09573c255798bddb6eb23c518afd
cases.defect: The new publish-spec gate looks for each migration's full filename in deploy-manifest [prod].migrations, which records bare versions, so the gate refuses every spec carrying a migration however thoroughly it was applied.
cases.evidence: supabase/deploy-manifest.json and scripts/stamp-deploy-manifest.sh (build_migrations_json), both unchanged. Comparison in the scripts/git-ops.sh hunk: base=$(basename "$m") then '$base' in prod.migrations.
cases.proof: Failure demonstration, run 2026-11-05 on the manifest at head: 310 entries, last three ['20260907180000','20260907190000','20260908100000'], zero ending in .sql, so a filename ending .sql is never a member.
cases.found_by: The gate refusing real work on another spec (fix message)
cases.why_chosen: A data-format mismatch across files; the failure path looks healthy.

cases.head: ceb0792291260e19cab5d4ca863c5f2fce1ad995
cases.defect: The new gate blocks any staged file over 500KB and exempts only package-lock.json, while the append-only docs/decisions.md is already about 4.2MB, so every commit recording a decision is refused.
cases.evidence: docs/decisions.md size at head, an unchanged file. Gate in the hunk, scripts/pre-commit-checks.sh:1079-1087.
cases.proof: Failure demonstration, run 2026-11-05: git show <head>:docs/decisions.md | wc -c gives 4233416, over the 512000 limit; the filter is only grep -vxF 'package-lock.json'.
cases.why_chosen: The evidence is a file's size rather than its text. A shell can see it; neither A nor C can, so this case favours D, and the report states so.

cases.head: ca9c0bd465dc86ede4e70872b3eb4484d3316ee5
cases.defect: stripHashtags ends with .replace(/\s{2,}/g, ' '). \s includes newlines, so every blank line in a tagged story collapses and multi-paragraph stories render as one block.
cases.proof: Failure demonstration, run 2026-11-05 in node: 'First para.\n\nSecond para. #tag'.replace(/\s{2,}/g,' ') gives 'First para. Second para. #tag'.
cases.found_by: The founder on a live story (fix message)
cases.why_chosen: One regex, fully in the hunk.

cases.head: d0b6708d7f514e80c137756651a40d9cdc6cb62d
cases.defect: The commit inserts pn between type and branch in the review stamp written by /dev, /fix and /finish, while the gate's branch arm in the same diff still requires "type":"code","branch":... to be adjacent, so a correctly recorded review is reported missing.
cases.evidence: scripts/ship-gates.sh branch-arm grep and .claude/commands/slava/build/dev.md stamp line, both in the hunks.
cases.proof: Failure demonstration, run 2026-11-05: piping {"type":"code","pn":"p1","branch":"feature/x","sha":"a"} into grep -E '"type": ?"code", ?"branch": ?"feature/x"' gives rc=1.
cases.why_chosen: Joining two hunks in different file types, while staying diff-only.

cases.head: ed91d7b6b985177f080c96e8a1824176f0416ac4
cases.defect: The new staging loop ( for f in ...; do [[ -e "$f" ]] && git add -- "$f"; done ) >&2 || exit 1 returns 1 when its last path is absent from disk, so a commit whose last path is a staged deletion, which the validation loop above explicitly accepts, dies with no message.
cases.evidence: scripts/git-ops.sh staging loop in cmd_commit_to_main, in the hunk, directly after the validation loop.
cases.proof: Failure demonstration, run 2026-11-05: bash -c 'set -e; ( for f in /nonexistent; do [[ -e "$f" ]] && echo add; done ) || { echo "ABORT rc=$?"; exit 1; }; echo reached' prints ABORT rc=1 and exits 1.
cases.found_by: Deletion-only batches exiting 1 under P1217 (fix message)
cases.why_chosen: Shell semantics fully in the hunk; a control against CF-3.
